mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >-0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising at an annualized rate above 3%, inflationary pressures erode real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 900,000 units for six consecutive months signals a housing market contraction, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on overall market returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, labor market tightness increases, pushing wage inflation and input costs higher, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 3% YoY and 2% YoY respectively signals a synchronized expansion in demand and labor input, which boosts corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.
